run_note: Continuation run. The first numbers miner (cut off by the usage limit) had adopted the quota-page rows for VPC and subnets, Elastic IP, Gateways (except carrier gateways), Network ACLs, Network interfaces per Region, Route tables, Security groups and NAU, plus NAT capacity, public IPv4 and billing-code facts. d002.note: Source footnote: newer accounts can access two Availability Zones in US West (N. California). Accounts created from November 2025 get a uniform code mapping in the oldest Regions.

d016.note: 251 usable in a /24 is derived (needs a derive vote). The role of the first address (network address) is stated only in a 3-word list item that M4 rejects, so the claim names the other four roles.

d029.note: Contradiction: the VPC FAQ (tier 2) says the VPC IPv6 block is fixed at /56 and the subnet at /64 (vpc-faq-ipv6-vpc-fixed-56, vpc-faq-ipv6-subnet-fixed-64). The user guide (tier 1) says /44 to /60 for a VPC and /44 to /64 for a subnet, in increments of /4; the Amazon-provided block is a fixed /56. Teach the guide; the FAQ facts should be scoped or rejected by the registrar.

d071.note: Three zonal NAT gateways (3 x $0.045 per hour) and one Regional NAT gateway across three AZs ($0.135 per hour) cost the same per hour in the Ohio example; writers can show this with the two price facts.

d094.note: Source differs from the demand item: many Linux kernels use 32768-61000 (not 32768-60999), and a NAT gateway uses 1024-65535 (not 49152-65535). The guide's example ACL uses 32768-65535.
